jobs.description: THE ASSOCIATE ROLE The Associate is the operational lead on LAS engagements and a genuine thought partner in the advisory process. Associates transform leadership data into business-relevant insights: identifying patterns in people and teams, determining what those patterns mean for organizational outcomes, and communicating those implications in ways that help clients make better talent decisions. Associates own workstreams end-to-end. They drive the project plan, conduct and support interviews and assessments, synthesize qualitative and quantitative data, write the reports and client materials, and keep engagements moving. They partner closely with Consultants, who own the client relationship and the final deliverable, while taking real accountability for quality, pace, and the client experience along the way. This is a role with meaningful ownership. It is also a support role in an apprenticeship model: Associates build credibility, judgment, and client exposure over time, and responsibility grows as that credibility is earned. WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY DO The work varies by Solution and by team, but the following responsibilities are consistent across the role. Insight development and client deliverables Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data from interviews, assessments, diagnostics, and secondary research to identify themes, insights, and implications Write and own client deliverables, Advanced Leadership Profile (ALP) and Leadership Profile (LP) assessment reports, group and comparison reports, culture and team diagnostic outputs, board materials, workshop decks, and executive summaries Draft assessment components independently, including Individual Style Profile (ISP), 360, capabilities, strengths and development opportunities, and summary pages; over time, contribute Executive Intelligence (ExI) insights Connect leadership insight to business context, company performance, value creation, role requirements, and the risks and opportunities facing the client Assessment, interviews, and client interaction Conduct and support executive and stakeholder interviews; lead, co-lead, or participate in assessments depending on the Solution, the engagement, and the Consultant Conduct 360 reference interviews and synthesize input into balanced, evidence-based summaries Lead internal calibration calls and contribute an informed, data-backed point of view on scoring and conclusions Participate in client debriefs, workshops, and readouts; over time, debrief participants and lead segments of client sessions Administer proprietary leadership advisory tools and diagnostics (ISP, culture, team effectiveness, and related instruments) in partnership with the Consultant, and analyze the resulting data Represent the Firm with professionalism, maturity, and poise in written, verbal, virtual, and in-person settings, and handle confidential information with discretion Engagement and project management Own the project plan and timeline end-to-end; organize and facilitate team touchpoints, including kick-offs, check-ins, and project recaps Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for the client alongside the Consultant, and draft client and stakeholder communications Organize and distribute work across the engagement team, clarify roles, and hold the team accountable to deadlines Anticipate what the client, Consultant, and team will need next; identify risks early, escalate appropriately, and propose a path forward Synthesize client meetings, board interactions, and workshops into clear themes, decisions, and next steps Manage several engagements at once across time zones and competing deadlines, and maintain your capacity tracker accurately so staffing decisions can be made well Use AI-enabled tools thoughtfully to improve efficiency in research, drafting, and summarization, always validating sources and conclusions, exercising judgment around client data and confidentiality, and retaining human accountability for the insight Developing others and building the practice Guide Analysts on first-draft documents, provide examples and standards, and give timely, constructive feedback Serve as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor to new colleagues and contribute to their integration Contribute to Solution and intellectual capital development, case studies, best practices, and internal tools Build relationships with Executive Search colleagues and help them understand where LAS can add value for their clients Occasionally support business development, contributing to qualifications decks, proposal materials, and background research. Associates are rarely involved in client pitches; that exposure typically comes at the Senior Associate level and beyond. YOUR FIRST YEAR We invest heavily in structured onboarding, and we expect training to take priority over client work in the early months. New Associates are not expected to take a project solo until they have demonstrated proficiency in that skill under the mentorship of an experienced colleague. A typical first-year path includes: Firm and LAS onboarding — understanding our business model, strategy, services, and how Search and LAS work together. Core curriculum — Insight Foundations, Insight Bootcamp, Overview of Capabilities, Culture in Action, the Leadership Model, the 360s course, Writing with Impact, and ExI Bootcamp. Assessment — shadow full ALPs; lead 360 interviews and write the page solo; write ISP and capabilities pages; write strengths, development opportunities, and summary pages; build toward delivering a full ALP report at roughly 80 percent client readiness. Organizational consulting — administer and analyze ISP, culture, and team effectiveness surveys; draft group and culture reports; debrief the culture graph; support workshop design, materials, and onsite coordination. Business acumen — how businesses make money, different operating and ownership models, organizational structures, C-suite roles and responsibilities, and basic financial literacy. This is supported by the LAS Business Acumen Series (Business Strategy, Financial Basics, Anatomy of a Company, Engagement and Client Management). Consulting skills — craft a credible introduction for clients, present informed opinions and defend them with data, professionally challenge the views of others, and proactively seek feedback from every project team. THE SUPPORT AROUND YOU You will not be left to figure this out alone. Every new Associate is supported by a defined team: Talent Partner — your manager, responsible for your development, staffing, and performance, with a recurring one-on-one cadence Onboarding mentor — a peer who helps you navigate the Firm, its systems, and its unwritten rules Apprenticeship mentors — one to two Associates or Senior Associates who are your first point of contact for client work; new hires are paired with a dedicated Consultant or Senior Associate capacity for the first six to twelve months, so you learn by apprenticeship Engagement teams — Consultants, Associates, and Executive Engagement Assistants who coach you in the flow of the work The AAPM community — the Associate & Analyst Practice Member group, which runs monthly calls, coffee chats, learning cafés, and peer development programming THE REALITIES OF THE ROLE We would rather be direct than have you discover these after you join. The workload is deadline-driven and uneven. Priorities are set by client needs and Consultant schedules. There are genuinely intense stretches around report deadlines, board readouts, and workshops, and quieter stretches in between. This is client service: timelines shift, clients reschedule, and there will be occasional work outside normal hours to meet a client commitment. Assessment work is rigorous. Spending several hours on camera with a participant and then multiple hours writing and nuancing a report is demanding. It is also core to what we do. We balance assessment with other work to give you a variety. Staffing is partially relationship-based. Opportunities are influenced by the connections, trust, and internal reputation you build. Early on, you will work on what the practice needs, which may not always be the work that energizes you most. Over time, you gain far more influence over the projects and people you work with, but you have to invest in the relationships to get there. The work is predominantly at the most senior levels. Because we work with C-suite executives and boards, there are fewer opportunities to independently lead assessments early on than at firms that work deeper in the organization. This also leads to what makes the role great (below). Autonomy can feel like ambiguity. You will be trusted to manage your own time and to choose work in partnership with your Talent Partner. Not every step will be laid out for you. The learning curve is real. Our methodology is complex, and our quality bar is high. Most Associates, including those with directly relevant prior experience, need several months before they feel confident with the tools, frameworks, and standards. That is expected. WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE WORTH IT Exposure to senior leaders and consequential decisions. Associates work directly on material that reaches C-suite executives, boards, and investors, and contributes to decisions that shape organizations. That exposure typically comes much later in a career elsewhere. Accelerated learning. You will see how successful leaders think, make decisions, and navigate complexity across many companies, industries, and situations in a fraction of the time it would take from inside a single organization. Exceptional colleagues. Our people are consistently named as the best part of working here: smart, generous with their time, deeply committed to quality, and invested in helping one another improve. Quality over volume. We prioritize thoughtful analysis, sound judgment, and exceptional work products over speed or scale. That creates a steeper learning curve and a far better development experience. Variety and breadth. Public and private companies across every major sector, and work spanning assessment, succession, culture, team effectiveness, development, and organizational effectiveness. Real ownership. You own workstreams, deliverables and client communications, and you have meaningful influence over your schedule, your projects and your career path. A developmental culture. Structured curriculum, apprenticeship mentoring, real-time feedback on every project, a published development framework and colleagues who are invested in your growth rather than competing with you. KEY RELATIONSHIPS Reports to Talent Partner (Leadership Advisory Services) Day-to-day direction Consultants and Senior Associates, on a per-engagement basis Career guidance Counselor (Consultant), onboarding mentor and apprenticeship mentors Other key relationships Analysts; Project Managers; Executive Engagement Assistants; Content Editors; Client Care Liaisons; Knowledge Management and Solution Support; Executive Search colleagues; the Associate & Analyst Practice Member (AAPM) community Location Based in one of our North American offices CANDIDATE PROFILE IDEAL EXPERIENCE Generally four or more years of relevant professional experience in leadership advisory, executive assessment, management or strategy consulting, organizational development, human capital or talent management, or a relevant industry role. Undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. An advanced degree (for example, in organizational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, business or a related field) is helpful but not required; relevant professional experience can substitute. Superior business writing skills, evidenced through project work or a writing sample provided on request Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information into clear, evidence-based insight Strong project management and organizational skills, with a track record of managing multiple priorities and competing deadlines General business acumen developed through exposure to a range of business situations and contexts Executive presence and interpersonal effectiveness; comfort interacting with senior leaders Client deliverables are written in English; superior English business writing is an essential function of the role. Additional languages are an advantage. Work authorization for the country in which you are applying WHO TENDS TO THRIVE HERE Intellectually curious people who want to understand the “why” behind people, businesses, and organizational outcomes, and who enjoy connecting disparate pieces of information into a point of view People who combine intellectual confidence with genuine humility, and who engage readily with feedback and iteration Strong writers and communicators who take visible pride in the quality of their work and the accuracy of their details Self-directed people who are comfortable creating structure where none exists, figuring things out independently, and taking ownership of their own career Resourceful relationship builders who proactively reach out, build trust across teams, and adapt their style to different personalities and Consultant preferences People who are comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and the pace of client service Team-oriented colleagues with a “no task too small” mindset who contribute beyond their immediate responsibilities People with poise, maturity, and professional presence IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU? We would rather you have a clear picture now than discover it after you join. The role consistently requires the following. If these conditions do not match what you are looking for, this may not be the right fit: Earned scope rather than immediate ownership . Client relationship ownership and independent assessment leadership expand as demonstrated quality and trust are established, not from day one. Working without a defined process . Engagements vary by Solution, client, and Consultant. The role requires building your own structure, workflows, and standards in the absence of fixed procedures. Extensive writing and multiple revision cycles . Writing is an essential function. Deliverables routinely undergo several rounds of substantive feedback and rework before reaching the client. Owning your own project management . The role carries end-to-end accountability for timelines, coordination, and follow-up. Dedicated project management support is not provided. Building internal relationships that influence staffing . Engagement assignments are shaped in part by internal trust and reputation, which the role requires you to actively develop. Capability-based advancement . Progression to Consultant is assessed against a published framework and takes time; it is not tenure-driven or accelerated on request. Limited early opportunity to independently lead assessments . Because our work sits at the C-suite and board level, independent assessment leadership comes later than at firms working deeper in the organization. Influence through partnership rather than sole authority . Decisions are reached collaboratively with Consultants and engagement teams. A distinct business from Executive Search . LAS has different client work, methodologies, and career paths. CRITICAL CAPABILITIES FOR SUCCESS These capabilities form the basis of the LAS Associate Development Framework and of the assessment of performance and promotion readiness. We share them openly so you know what you are signing up for and how you will be evaluated. Project management Manages overall projects and oversees the team's collective efforts to drive the cadence and flow of client outcomes. Owns the project workplan across multiple workstreams; organizes and facilitates team touchpoints and keeps the team accountable Takes ownership of whole projects and serves as a day-to-day point of contact with the client Manages multiple engagements with competing deadlines; sets expectations, clarifies roles, and avoids duplication of effort Anticipates challenges, adjusts priorities, and pushes back internally as appropriate Remains calm under pressure and delivers on commitments, or raises slippage early with a proposed solution Uses technology and AI-enabled tools to improve project efficiency, with appropriate validation Client insights Gathers nuanced insight from sophisticated data collection and delivers it in a way that is relevant for clients and resonates with participants. Co-administers our tools and develops independent insights under the supervision of a Consultant or more experienced colleague; knows how each tool relates to the others and to our overall methodology Elevates perspective to discern themes across individuals and deliver nuanced insight at the team or organizational level Highlights and resolves inconsistencies or contradictions in the data to reach a more nuanced narrative Produces client-ready documents, assessment reports, comparison reports, and board decks with limited assistance Conveys insight compellingly, beyond “just the facts,” tailored to the audience and the client situation Engages in constructive discussion with the Consultant, defending a view and amending it when the evidence warrants Impact and effectiveness Communicates effectively in writing and verbally; has executive presence and builds trusted relationships. Establishes productive relationships with clients, participants, and colleagues across the Firm, and builds a personal brand defined by reliability and collaboration Adapts style to the audience, coaching with participants, business-insight-driven with clients, and remains composed under pressure Contributes meaningfully in debriefs, assessments, workshops, and client conversations without being prompted Coordinates team efforts on complex projects; unblocks obstacles and helps create consensus Places team goals ahead of individual goals; volunteers to share workload and shares information generously while being rigorous about confidentiality Business and market knowledge Obtains and incorporates knowledge across one or more of our Solutions to enhance client work in a meaningful way. Builds deep knowledge of the concepts and principles underlying our assessment, culture, team, development, succession, and performance acceleration frameworks, and can teach others Develops foundational business acumen, financial statements, executive role responsibilities, organizational structures, and operating models, and applies them to the client context Shows curiosity about the bigger picture surrounding an assignment, taking a systems view that considers company and industry context Understands how Search and LAS work together, and navigates internal resources, materials, and experts to bring the best of the Firm to client work Stays current on business, economic, and leadership advisory news, and brings relevant insight to teams and clients Developing self and others Seeks and provides feedback; coaches and mentors to improve team performance; modifies own performance based on input. Proactively seeks feedback from every project team and demonstrates progress against development areas over time Takes personal responsibility for career development, engaging mentors and sponsors, and articulating aspirations clearly Provides balanced, behavioral feedback to junior colleagues and creates opportunities for their development Serves as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor and supports the integration of new colleagues Firm values Champions the Firm's values, culture, and Code of Conduct; engages, participates, and collaborates with others. Demonstrates alignment to Firm values in everyday behavior; is professional, cordial, and engaging in all settings Brings cultural awareness and sensitivity to every interaction with colleagues and clients Participates actively in office, practice, and Firm-wide activities, and builds a network beyond LAS Leverages AI responsibly, maintaining human accountability for client data, confidential information, and intellectual property Represents Spencer Stuart well and lives by the Code of Conduct Career path and progression Level: Associate What changes: Own workstreams end-to-end; manage substantial project components with increasing autonomy; build trusted client relationships; synthesize data into clear, client-relevant insight; create structure from ambiguity; begin developing others intentionally. Typical review cadence: Entry point Level: Senior Associate What changes: Lead client interactions and complex, multi-Solution programs; deepen advisory expertise; progress toward Associate Consultant and Consultant roles or to other internal opportunities across the Firm. Typical review cadence: Reviewed twice per year Level: Associate Consultant and beyond What changes: Advise clients in the first seat; develop distinctive Solution or industry expertise; support and originate commercial opportunities; progress toward the Consultant and Partner track or to other senior opportunities across the Firm. Typical review cadence: Reviewed annually Review cadence is typical, not guaranteed; promotion is capability-based and discretionary. Associates also pursue a range of paths beyond the LAS delivery track, including roles elsewhere in the Firm. HOW WE WORK Hybrid working. Colleagues are in the office a minimum of two days per week. For new hires, we strongly recommend three to four days per week during the early months, because learning, shadowing, and relationship-building happen fastest in person. Best practice is to choose the days your team is also in. Subject to reasonable accommodation. Staffing and autonomy. New Associates are paired with one to two Consultants or Senior Associates for their first six to twelve months. As your network develops, you take a greater role in choosing projects in partnership with your Talent Partner, weighing interests, developmental value, relationships, and goals. Travel. Travel is modest and has decreased as assessments have moved largely online. Expect roughly 25-50 percent at the high end, primarily for client workshops, onsite sessions, occasional board meetings, and Firm events, with considerable variation by Solution and team. Most associates travel less than 20% of their time. Flexibility. We are a client-service business. Timelines shift, and there will be occasional early, late or rescheduled work to meet a client commitment. In exchange, you have real control over how you manage the rest of your time. The base compensation range for this position is $100,000 –150,000 per year. The actual base compensation within the range above will be dependent on the individual’s skills, experiences, and qualifications. This position may be eligible to participate in our annual discretionary bonus program. Spencer Stuart also offers a competitive benefits package, which includes: Retirement savings plan with discretionary profit sharing contribution and employer match; PTO (minimum 15 days per year, increases with tenure), paid sick time (10 days per year), company holidays (12 days per year), and paid leaves of absence when applicable; Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, and healthcare flexible spending account; Life Insurance, and short-term and long-term disability insurance; Wellness benefits, including an employee assistance program, virtual mental health program, and mindfulness program; and Voluntary benefit options, including supplemental life insurance, identity theft protection, and whole life insurance with long-term care and critical illness coverage. jobs.description: At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet. Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place. About you and this role The Full Stack Developer is responsible for the design, development, implementation, support, and continuous improvement of enterprise business applications. This role partners with business stakeholders, solution managers, architects, and other technical teams to deliver scalable, secure, and high-quality digital solutions that enable critical business processes. The successful candidate will possess strong experience in Microsoft .NET technologies and Angular front-end development while contributing throughout the software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, technical design, development, testing, deployment, and production support. The role combines hands-on development with solution ownership and continuous improvement responsibilities. Developer is expected to manage solutions throughout their lifecycle and partner closely with business stakeholders to deliver business value. Responsibilities Solution Design & Development Design, develop, test, and support enterprise web applications using .NET and Angular technologies as well as development support for SAP BODS ETL related solutions. Create scalable, maintainable, and secure software solutions aligned with enterprise architecture standards. Develop REST APIs, web services, and system integrations. Participate in technical design reviews and solution architecture discussions. Ensure code quality through peer reviews, automated testing, and adherence to development standards. Application Lifecycle Management Support applications through their full lifecycle, including implementation, enhancement, maintenance, and retirement. Analyze business requirements and translate them into technical designs and functional solutions. Identify opportunities for automation, modernization, and process simplification. Participate in release planning, deployment activities, and production support. Operational Support Troubleshoot and resolve production incidents and application defects. Perform root cause analysis and implement long-term corrective actions. Collaborate with infrastructure, security, and business teams to ensure system reliability and performance. Monitor application health and proactively address technical debt. Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement Partner with business process owners, Solution Managers, and cross-functional teams to deliver business value. Participate in Agile ceremonies, backlog refinement, sprint planning, and retrospectives. Provide technical guidance and knowledge transfer to team members. Create and maintain technical documentation, support procedures, and system specifications. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science , Information Technology, Engineering, or related discipline. 3+ years of experience in software development and application support. Strong hands-on experience with: C# , ASP.NET Core / .NET Framework, Angular (Angular 12+ preferred) HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, TypeScript RESTful APIs and web services SQL Server and relational databases Experience with source control systems such as Git and Azure DevOps. Willingness to learn and support BODS data ETL in SAP Understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC) and Agile methodologies. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Your Skill s The following qualifications are considered a strong advantage: Experience with Azure cloud services and modern cloud-native application development. Experience with Azure DevOps pipelines, CI/CD automation, and infrastructure-as-code practices. Knowledge of enterprise integration patterns, APIs, and middleware technologies. Experience supporting finance, manufacturing, supply chain, or other enterprise business applications. Familiarity with SAP landscapes and business processes. Experience with Power Platform technologies (Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI). Bonus Skills / Nice to Have Experience with SAP BusinessObjects Data Services (BODS) development. Experience with SAP HANA database development, modeling, SQLScript Knowledge of SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA integration concepts. Willingness and aptitude to learn SAP BODS and SAP HANA development technologies if prior experience is not present. Experience supporting data integration, ETL processes, and enterprise data management solutions. Additional Notes The ability to accommodate a flexible schedule aligned with international time zones is essential. No Relocation support is provided on the role. Benefits – What Dow offers you We invest in you. Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing. Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee: Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives. Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it. Competitive retirement program that may include company-provided benefits, savings opportunities, financial planning, and educational resources to help you achieve your long term financial-goals. Employee stock purchase programs (availability varies depending on location). Student Debt Retirement Savings Match Program (U.S. only). Dow will take the value of monthly student debt payments and apply them as if they are contributions to the Employees’ Savings Plan (401(k)), helping employees reach the Company match. Robust medical and life insurance packages that offer a variety of coverage options to meet your individual needs. Travel insurance is also available in certain countries/locations. Opportunities to learn and grow through training and mentoring, work experiences, community involvement and team building. Workplace culture empowering role-based flexibility to maximize personal productivity and balance personal needs. Competitive yearly vacation allowance. Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents). Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured. Paid time off to support volunteering and Employee Resource Group’s (ERG) participation. Wellbeing Portal for all Dow employees, our one-stop shop to promote wellbeing, empowering employees to take ownership of their entire wellbeing journey. On-site fitness facilities to help stay healthy and active (availability varies depending on location). Employee discounts for online shopping, cinema tickets, gym memberships and more. Additionally, some of our locations might offer: Transportation allowance (availability varies depending on location) Meal subsidiaries/vouchers (availability varies depending on location) Carbon-neutral transportation incentives e.g. bike to work (availability varies depending on location) Join our team, we can make a difference together. About Dow Chemical International Pvt Ltd Dow Chemical International Private Limited (Dow India) aims to be the most innovative, sustainable, inclusive customer-centric materials science company. The company is committed to delivering the right solutions to its customers’ challenges. With broadest technology sets spanning performance materials, industrial intermediates, and plastics Dow India delivers differentiated science-based products and solutions in high-growth segments, such as packaging, infrastructure, automobile, and consumer care. A Great Place to Work® Certified company with approximately over 1000 employees, its operations comprise of manufacturing sites, innovation center, established centers of excellence, and commercial office. As a responsible corporate, the company supports its Corporate Social Responsibility (program) with technology expertise and employee volunteerism. Dow India works with non-profit partners towards the empowerment of differently abled, women, and children in communities where it operates. The company aims to redefine the societal blueprint, by supporting holistic sustainability and circular economy initiatives. As part of our dedication to inclusion, Dow is committed to equal opportunities in employment . We encourage every employee to bring their whole self to work each day to not only deliver more value, but also have a more fulfilling career. jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: With direct supervision from a Lead Technician, Fleet Maintenance Supervisor or Maintenance Manager, a Maintenance Technician A performs repair and maintenance work on diesel and non-diesel equipment and trucks including, but not limited to, chassis components; refuse bodies, including control, hydraulic, and electrical systems; air brake systems; general engine work; HVAC components; and suspension, drive train and steering systems. Enjoy the benefits of working on a single fleet with state-of-the-art equipment, supporting our drivers as they run their routes and servicing some of the most technically advanced vehicles on the road. Tackle a new challenge every day. Maintain and repair highly intricate and powerful machinery. Receive training in new technologies and equipment. Work a regular shift in a stable industry. Be recognized for exceptional performance. Serve your community and your customers. Follow strong career paths for professional growth. Enjoy competitive wages and benefits. Join us and help make a positive impact on your community, your environment, and your world. PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES: Maintains advanced knowledge of, and strong skill proficiency in, the following vehicle components and systems, with the ability to perform complex repair maintenance functions, on-site and on the road. Chassis component repair and maintenance. Refuse bodies, including control, hydraulic and electrical systems; Air and hydraulic braking systems. Engine repair and diagnostics . Complete understanding of diesel fuel systems and fuel systems diagnostics. Suspension, drivetrain and steering systems. Heating and air conditioning systems diagnostics and repair. Complete understanding of Aftertreatment systems, REGEN and diagnostics. Able to diagnose electrical concerns with scan tools. Line maintenance, welding and fabrication. Identifies the source of the malfunctions using a variety of electronic tools. Completes applicable Company training programs. Performs other job-related duties as assigned or apparent. QUALIFICATIONS: Ability to diagnose multi-system issues and consistently demonstrate technical expertise. 5 -7 years of experience as a technician working on heavy-duty trucks. Ability to perform inspections and repairs without supervision in some (not all required) of the following heavy truck, or automotive systems: Suspensions & Steering, General Engine, Transmissions, Brakes, Electrical, Hydraulics, Drive Train, Diesel Emissions. ASE Heavy Truck Certifications (T1-T8) are a plus but not required. LNG and/or CNG experience is a plus but not required. Class B or higher Commercial Driver’s License is a plus but not required. Preferred CDL B MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: Valid Driver’s License. Rewarding Compensation and Benefits Eligible employees can elect to participate in: • Comprehensive medical benefits coverage, dental plans and vision coverage. • Health care and dependent care spending accounts. • Short- and long-term disability. • Life insurance and accidental death & dismemberment insurance. • Employee and Family Assistance Program (EAP). • Employee discount programs. • Retirement plan with a generous company match. • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). • Paid Time Off (PTO) • Benefits: https://jobs.republicservices.com/us/en/about-us/benefits The statements used herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of the work being performed by an employee in this position, and are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties and skills required by an incumbent so classified. Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the Company. EEO STATEMENT:Republic Services is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, relationship or association with a protected veteran (spouses or other family members), genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4. ABOUT THE COMPANY Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world. In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills. Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer. Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it. Our company values guide our daily actions: Safe : We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities. Committed to Serve : We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations. Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment. Driven : We deliver results in the right way. Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person. We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods. STRATEGY Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets. We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation. With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers. Recycling and Waste We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs. Environmental Solutions Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. Scopely is looking for a Senior Producer to join the Live Game organisation supporting the MONOPOLY GO! team. This role is remote within the EU and will support our Barcelona and Sevilla hubs.
At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and strive to inspire play every day—through our work alongside talented colleagues and through our connection with millions of players around the world.
MONOPOLY GO! is one of Scopely’s flagship mobile free-to-play franchises and one of the largest games in the mobile industry.
With teams distributed across Barcelona, Sevilla, the United States, and other global locations, this role requires strong production leadership, excellent communication, and exceptional attention to detail.
About the Role
As a Senior Producer within the Live Game organization, you will oversee development across one or more live game workstreams, helping transform product strategy and creative goals into high-quality player experiences.
You will manage development from early planning and team alignment through implementation, integration, QA, release, and live support. This includes coordinating concurrent initiatives, managing complex dependency chains, driving change request flow, and ensuring teams remain focused on delivering meaningful player and business outcomes.
This is a hands-on, in-the-weeds production role requiring both strategic thinking and tactical execution. You will work closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Art, Content, Economy, QA, Localization, Analytics, Live Operations, and Release Management to deliver at the pace and quality expected of a global mobile live-service game.
What You Will Do
Own the end-to-end production lifecycle for assigned Live Game development workstreams, from discovery and planning through development, release, and post-launch support.
Manage multiple concurrent initiatives with shared teams, resources, dependencies, and shifting priorities.
Translate product strategy and roadmap objectives into clear, executable development plans.
Build and maintain integrated schedules, milestone plans, critical paths, risk registers, and dependency maps.
Coordinate development across Product, Game Design, Engineering, Art, Content, Economy, QA, Localization, Analytics, Live Operations, and Release Management.
Establish clear DRIs, requirements, acceptance criteria, decision points, and delivery expectations for major initiatives.
Manage the complete mobile live-service development lifecycle, including design alignment, implementation, configuration, integration, QA validation, release readiness, live activation, and post-launch follow-up.
Partner with Live Operations and Release Management to ensure development work is compatible with the LiveOps calendar, release cadence, player priorities, and operational requirements.
Lead the change request process by assessing the impact of proposed changes on scope, schedule, capacity, quality, risk, and downstream dependencies.
Drive prioritization and decision-making around change requests, communicate approved changes clearly, and ensure plans and systems remain aligned with the latest direction.
Proactively identify blockers, bottlenecks, gaps in ownership, and risks to delivery. Resolve issues directly where possible and escalate with clear recommendations when necessary.
Facilitate milestone reviews, sprint planning, production checkpoints, risk reviews, and cross-functional working sessions.
Ensure meetings result in clear decisions, owners, deadlines, and follow-through.
Maintain accurate and current project information across Jira, Airtable, Confluence, and other production systems.
Communicate project status, risks, dependencies, decisions, and delivery confidence clearly to both senior leadership and development teams across the Barcelona and Sevilla hubs.
Partner with Live Operations after launch to support issue triage, player-impacting investigations, post-launch actions, and continuous improvement.
Use player data, team feedback, and operational insights to inform prioritization and improve future development planning.
Champion improvements to development workflows, production practices, tooling, and cross-functional collaboration across the Live Game organization.
What We’re Looking For
5+ years of experience in game production, with significant experience in mobile free-to-play or live-service games.
Proven experience managing the development and delivery of mobile game features, systems, content, events, or other player-facing experiences.
Strong understanding of Live Operations, including high-frequency content delivery, live calendars, release cycles, remote configuration, QA validation, launch readiness, and post-launch support.
Experience managing multiple concurrent development workstreams with complex cross-functional dependencies.
Strong understanding of roadmap planning, milestone management, critical-path tracking, risk management, change management, and delivery readiness.
Experience partnering closely with Engineering and technical teams, with an understanding of client/server dependencies, configuration, integration, and mobile release considerations.
Demonstrated ability to manage dependency escalation, negotiate tradeoffs, and create accountability across teams.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to bring clarity to complex or ambiguous situations.
Exceptional attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership for the quality and accuracy of production information.
Proficiency with tools such as Jira, Airtable, Confluence, Google Workspace, or similar project-management systems.
Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels, from shaping a development roadmap to following individual deliverables through completion.
A player-focused mindset and passion for building engaging, polished, and continuously evolving mobile game experiences.
The Ideal Candidate
Is highly organized, structured, dependable, and comfortable operating in a high-volume Live Operations environment.
Understands the realities of mobile free-to-play development, including rapid iteration, global releases, frequent content updates, live player impact, and operational precision.
Drives outcomes beyond task tracking and status reporting.
Anticipates problems before they become delivery issues.
Communicates directly, diplomatically, and consistently across global teams and time zones.
Creates accountability without unnecessary process or bureaucracy.
Is comfortable challenging unclear plans, identifying gaps, and driving decisions.
Can manage competing priorities while maintaining focus on the critical path.
Brings sound judgment, energy, and a collaborative mindset to a fast-paced, globally distributed development organization.
Cares deeply about both the quality of the player experience and the operational excellence required to deliver it.
About Scopely
Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.
Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.
Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

jobs.description: About the Team The GPT Infrastructure team builds systems that turn advances in model inference and optimization into reliable production capabilities. You will work across model architecture, distributed execution, compilers, runtimes, networking, and accelerator systems. A central part of the role is turning research prototypes and one-off hardware bring-up efforts into reliable, reusable infrastructure with clear contracts, reproducible results, strong observability, and well-defined security boundaries.
